newsitem.title: UK: British-Borneo in rights issue, U.S. buy.
newsitem.headline: British-Borneo in rights issue, U.S. buy.

text.p: British-Borneo Petroleum Syndicate Plc said on Wednesday it planned a two-for-nine rights issue of shares at 1,200p per share to raise a net 167.3 million stg.

The company said it had agreed to buy from Conoco its 50 percent interest in blocks in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico which contain the King Kong gas field. British-Borneo also forecast a full-year dividend of 8.25p and announced a reorganisation of its share capital.
The rights issue price compares with a close on Tuesday of 1,412-1/2p.
British-Borneo said the Conoco interests it is buying are in contiguous blocks Green Canyon 472, 473 and 517.
It said in a statement it proposes to reorganise its share capital of, following completion of the rights issue, resulting in three consolidated shares of 50p for every one share of 10p.
British-Borneo said it had an exciting exploration and development programme and estimated that over the four year period to the end of 2000, capital expenditure was likely to exceed 500 million stg.

"Accordingly, the board believes it is now appropriate to strengthen the permanent equity base of the company to support an increasing level of operational activity, to enhance the company's credibility with potential partners and to improve access to the debt markets for the financing of development expenditure," it said.

Chief executive Alan Gaynor said: "We believe it is now appropriate to increase our capital base in order to fund efficiently our very substantial capital expenditure programme, enabling us to fully exploit our asset portfolio and capture new business opportunities."

"The acquisition of the interest in King Kong further demonstrates British-Borneo's ability to exploit its position in the Gulf of Mexico to secure deals with major oil and gas companies; it represents for us a significant gas field which should provide an attractive revenue stream in the medium term whilst also offering further exploration potential," he said in the statement.
The rights issue is underwritten by N.M. Rothschild and brokers to the issue are Cazenove & Co and HSBC James Capel.
